summary: The layout and ownership rules are clear enough to start, but the build mechanics are not: the biggest gap is how vendor/MicroHs and the shared/SDK sources actually enter the native and guest builds.

questions.text: Does the native build link vendor/MicroHs as a Cabal library or build and run it as a separate compiler binary?
questions.reason: Decides cabal.project, kyyn-microhs dependencies and how its interpreters invoke the compiler; the ADR only requires one vendored revision for both native integration and the guest toolchain.

questions.text: Are guest/kyyn-sdk and guest/kyyn-runtime Cabal packages built and tested by GHC via cabal.project, or MicroHs-only?
questions.reason: Fixes package boundaries, which compilers the guest source must support and what GHC tests cover; the ADR says only that not every guest dependency must be a native Cabal package.

questions.text: How does the shared/kyyn-types source physically reach the MicroHs SDK build: package dependency, cross-directory search path, or a staged copy?
questions.reason: Determines the single-source guarantee and SDK build setup; the ADR says host and SDK compile the same source but not how the guest build references it.

questions.text: What rule decides whether a pure capability helper (decoders, binding generation, contract projections) lives in kyyn-plumbing or kyyn-porcelain-interpreters?
questions.reason: Ownership decides who may import helpers, e.g. whether kyyn-microhs's catalogue can use binding generation without a porcelain dependency; the ADR places helpers in both packages without a deciding rule.

questions.text: Are package boundaries enforced by Cabal build-depends and exposed modules alone, or by a separate module-level import checker gating CI?
questions.reason: Some rules (no helpers exported from interpreter modules, no native IO in porcelain interpreters) are module-level; the ADR only says package visibility and import checks must enforce ADR 0003.

questions.text: How does the installed MicroHs toolchain find kyyn-types, kyyn-sdk and kyyn-runtime when compiling guest code: precompiled packages, a search path, or source vendored into each KB?
questions.reason: Changes package.sh, test-guest.sh, integration fixtures and the upgrade story; the ADR says only that package.sh bundles the runtime/toolchain.

questions.text: Which step stages the runtime inputs kyyn-api-catalogue reads, and what are its relative paths relative to?
questions.reason: Sets the tool's CLI contract and build step ordering; the ADR says only that it inspects staged inputs from host/kyyn-microhs/app/ using relative paths.

questions.text: Should tools/test.sh fail or skip when a needed toolchain (built MicroHs, Node.js) is missing, and what makes a check applicable?
questions.reason: Determines developer and CI prerequisites and whether incomplete runs are reported; the ADR forbids silently skipping guest/plugin failures but leaves absent toolchains and Web checks undefined.

questions.text: Which libraries beyond base may shared/kyyn-types depend on, and who approves additions?
questions.reason: Fixes the shared vocabulary's data shapes (Text/Map vs String/lists, codec instances); the ADR gives only the rule 'pure libraries supported by both toolchains', checked in CI.

questions.text: Which way does the dependency run between kyyn-microhs and kyyn-plumbing-interpreters, and where does kyyn-microhs get its process and filesystem IO?
questions.reason: Avoids a package cycle and locates shared IO helpers; the ADR allows native plumbing interpreter packages to depend on kyyn-microhs but not the reverse question.

questions.text: Which package owns the type of the execution-function bundle kyyn-surfaces receives from kyyn?
questions.reason: kyyn depends on surfaces, so the type cannot live in kyyn without a cycle; the ADR says only that surfaces receives execution functions from kyyn.

questions.text: What is the dependency direction between kyyn-sdk and kyyn-runtime, given SDK-private observation constructors?
questions.reason: Decides whether the SDK needs an internal module MicroHs must keep hidden; the ADR keeps constructors in the SDK and says neither depends on the kernel, nothing about each other.

questions.text: Are generated guest bindings and the API catalogue committed with a freshness check, or produced only at build time?
questions.reason: Changes every build path and test gate; the ADR calls generated bindings derived artifacts but not whether they are committed.
